source.publication: Instructions for 2025 PIT-ADJ; 2025 PIT-1 Personal Income Tax Return Instructions; 2025 Tax Rate Table (Tax Look Up Table)
source.section: PIT-ADJ instructions PDF page 7, line 24; Form PIT-1 lines 9 to 18 and 22; instructions PDF page 25, line 12; Tax Rate Table PDF pages 1 to 6, rows; PDF page 7 (T-7), over 100,000

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 30,000.00 + armed forces retirement pay (person 0) 45,000.00 + armed forces retirement pay (person 1) 10,000.00 = 85,000.00. Federal taxable income = 85,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 53,500.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, married filing jointly. Line 9 federal AGI 85,000.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions 0.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 31,500.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 0.00: federal AGI 85,000.00 is over the worksheet's printed ceiling 55,000.00 for this status, so the worksheet is not completed. Line 15, PIT-ADJ: line 24 armed forces retirement pay (person 0): smaller of 45,000.00 and 30,000.00 = 30,000.00; line 24 armed forces retirement pay (person 1): smaller of 10,000.00 and 30,000.00 = 10,000.00; PIT-ADJ line 28 total 40,000.00. Line 17 = 85,000.00 + 0.00 - 31,500.00 - 0.00 - 40,000.00 = 13,500.00. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income 53,500.00 - 40,000.00 = 13,500.00; less base deductions 0.00 gives 13,500.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 8,000.00 = 120 + 3.2% x 5,500.00 = 176; total 296, to the cent 296.00. The table row over 13,400 to 13,500 gives 294; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 19 to 21 0.00. Line 22 net New Mexico income tax 296.00. The cap is each retiree's: person 0's unused excess does not move to person 1's room. Total 40,000.00, not 55,000.00.
